binding_contract.agentmemory_binding_is_empty: its mechanism was already exercised; the only variable moved for it is the fixture ingest order

agentmemory.effect: isLatest=false; the record stays in KV and leaves the search index. Absence from search is not deletion
agentmemory.issued: automatically on write, exactly as in Round 2
agentmemory.one_variable: NOTHING changes for this engine. Its mechanism was already exercised; the only variable Gen101 moves for it is the fixture's ingest order

arguments.reason: benchmark: superseded by the later observation

hindsight.effect: the observation's lifecycle state changes; its text is NOT replaced and the record is not deleted
hindsight.issued: once, after both records are written
hindsight.note: the only states the pinned build accepts are 'valid' and 'invalidated'; there is no 'supersedes' relationship to name, so this is a state transition and is labelled as one
hindsight.one_variable: retain and recall are unchanged; only the frozen 'lifecycle_calls: none' becomes this single call

mem0.effect: mem0's own consolidation decides; the harness selects nothing and issues no update or delete
mem0.issued: on every write; the engine decides whether a new statement updates an earlier one
mem0.note: Memory.update exists and is NOT used: it would replace the old record's content, which is the harness deciding the outcome rather than the engine
mem0.one_variable: infer flips from False to True and nothing else moves

arguments.reason: benchmark: the later observation replaces the earlier

perseus.effect: the old entity's status becomes 'deprecated'; it is not removed
perseus.issued: once, after both records are written
perseus.one_variable: the frozen Gen29 write path is unchanged; this is the only added call

binding_contract.mechanism_kinds_are_not_equivalent: explicit lineage, a state transition and a product decision are three different things; reporting them as one comparison would manufacture an equivalence the interfaces do not support
binding_contract.nothing_deletes: every binding leaves the superseded record in the store; assert_no_deletion refuses one that does not

fixture_contract.single_change: the ingest order: the superseded record is written FIRST and the current record SECOND
unchanged: the foreign record on both axes
fixture_contract.v2_not_rewritten: interference_v2 is untouched; its hashes stay valid for every committed Gen99 result, and the defect stays on the record
fixture_contract.why: v2's order was backwards from the world it models, and agentmemory's write-time rule - which retires the older near-duplicate - therefore retired the record we meant to keep (Gen100)
